[context_summary]
We are helping a user solve: a video at /app/video.mp4 shows someone playing "Zork" (a text adventure). Task: (1) transcribe the entire contents of the text visible in the video, and (2) create /app/solution.txt containing all the moves the player input, one per line (e.g., 'n', 'get bag', etc.).

Environment/tooling established:
- Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, Python 3.12, no ffmpeg/pip initially. Installed ffmpeg, tesseract-ocr, python3-pil, imagemagick via apt. pip is externally managed (use --break-system-packages or apt packages).
- Video is 1280x720, 30fps, ~190.1s. Extracted frames at 1fps (/app/frames, 190 frames) and 5fps (/app/frames5, 951 frames). OCR'd all 5fps frames into /app/ocr5/ocr_NNNN.txt over ~23 min.
- The screen: top header line "West of House Score: N Moves: N"; below is the scrolling game transcript. OCR works well on full frames (psm 6).
- Generated helper files: /app/prompts_per_frame.txt (per-frame ">" prompt lines), /app/last_prompt.txt (per-frame newest prompt), /app/timeline_tail.txt, /app/moves1fps.txt (unreliable header OCR at 1fps).

Learnings about the game content:
- The player played a nearly complete ZORK I game reaching the final ending screen: "Your score is 350 (total of 350 points), in 262 moves. This gives you the rank of Master Adventurer." So there should be exactly 262 commands.
- The 5fps OCR captured the full gameplay. Commands are lines starting with ">" in the transcript; partial typing appears as growing prefixes across frames (e.g., ">s"→">sw"→">swW"); the completed command is the maximal form followed by a response.
- Reconstructed early command sequence so far (order matters, exact move numbers uncertain): n, n, u, get egg, d, s, e, open, w, get all, move rug, open case, open trap, d, light lamp, s, e, get, w,
[/context_summary]
